findings.text: Boot entry scans PCI bus zero when early PCI access is permitted, walking every slot and function and delegating per-device work to a matcher that also follows bridge secondary buses.

Per-device matcher ignores absent class codes, matches vendor and device with wildcard support plus masked class equality, invokes the registered handler unless once-only done bits are already set, then marks applied, recurses into higher numbered secondary buses for bridges, and requests single-function stop when multifunction bit is clear.
Quirk table entry carries vendor id, device id, class code, class mask, flag bits, and a callback receiving bus slot and function numbers.
Graphics helper bundle holds two callbacks with bus slot function parameters, one returning stolen size and one returning stolen base given that size.

Table pairs bridge, host, display, serial and network classes with handlers for timer override, interconnect, remapping check, graphics reservation, timer disable and wireless reset, with two entries limited to single application and terminated by an empty entry.
Remapping health check marks remapping broken when revision is at or below 0x13, or for one specific device value at one specific later revision.

First timer path exits when forced override is set, otherwise derives a low byte revision after config updates, forces skip on revisions below 0x82, otherwise probes an indexed port pair and forces skip when a swap bit is clear, emitting informational messages when skipping.

Second timer path records revision, enables pin polarity fix at or above 0x40, exits at or above 0x39, otherwise unless forced override checks a config bit for swap and enables skip with informational messages when skipping.
Alternate builds provide empty timer handlers that perform no config access and change no override state.

Segment and memory sizing is enable gated, returning zero when disabled, else fixed small sizes selected by register bits with a warning on unknown encodings, and total memory from a fixed bus device register scaled by thirty two megabytes.

Stolen base is computed per generation either by subtracting segment and stolen sizes from total memory, by scaling a top-of-memory register and adding segment size, or by reading and masking a stolen base register with a newer variant combining low and high halves into sixty four bits.

Stolen size decodes a control field into fixed megabyte values for older generations with warnings on unknown codes and zero for local memory, linear thirty two megabyte steps for middle generations, and piecewise linear formulas with small megabyte granularity for newer variants.
Device table associates many integrated graphics families with one of ten prebuilt helper bundles combining a base routine and a size routine, alongside a global stolen resource initially empty.

Graphics quirk runs at most once per boot, matches current device by identifier, queries size then base through paired helpers, ignores zero results, otherwise stores inclusive start and end in the global resource, logs the reservation, and marks the range reserved in the firmware memory map before refreshing the table.
Baytrail path conditionally sets a boot flag requesting timer disable and logs that the timer is unreliable on this platform.

Wireless reset runs only on Apple hardware, restores power state to D0 with delay and verification, maps a fixed length window at the masked address, waits bounded for idle status, pulses reset control with interleaved reads and microdelays, then unmaps.

VGA early output maintains an eighty by twenty five cursor starting at the bottom line, scrolls by copying rows upward and clearing the last row with a fixed attribute when full, handles newline and carriage return, emits other characters with grey attribute and wraps lines, with optional backspace handling in one build.

Serial facts: default base 0x3f8, offsets zero through six for data interrupt identification control modem and status roles with shared encodings, transmitter ready bit 0x20, divisor latch bit 0x80; helpers add offset to base for byte port access.
Flag facts: apply once is 0x1, applied is 0x2, done is their union; wireless window is 16384 bytes with power capability at 0x40; kilobyte scales by 1024 and megabyte by nested kilobyte scaling.
Visible boot services are the top level quirk entry callable during early init and the global stolen graphics range updated once and thereafter effectively read only.

Early paths perform raw config writes, indexed port reads, and memory mapped resets without shown locking, assume single threaded boot context, depend on successful early mapping before register polling, and write directly to fixed video memory assuming identity mapping.
